correctness.rationale: For any binary seed beginning 010, one-symbol prefix duplication moves into the forward-invariant 00-prefix sector; the only transitions retaining prefix 01 prepend 01 or 010. Gaps between consecutive 1 symbols before the identified suffix uniquely recover the complete block sequence and therefore every derivation. Each block contributes one 1, proving exact distance and the bivariate geometric-series formula. Same-parity Fibonacci suffixes and two-or-three gaps supply the all-pairs corollary. Sharp four-bounded witnesses were checked directly. The standalone forward-path enumerator (1750 targets), independent reverse dynamic program (63 Fibonacci pairs), and boundary tests passed; infinite assertions rest on the proof.

originality.rationale: The July 2026 full text proves existence of Fibonacci derivations, but not a universal regular-language normal form or uniqueness. Its companion implementation claims shortest Fibonacci derivations, which algorithmically addresses the special case but does not give an arbitrary-seed uniqueness theorem or the length-distance generating series. Earlier general-distance and regular-closure papers give broad algorithms but no identified equivalence in accessible material; incomplete access is recorded as residual risk rather than represented as a complete check.
residual_risks: The 2014 bounded-duplication primary PDF was not accessible in full; equivalent special results in uninspected text remain possible.
The 2014 general duplication-distance article was only partially accessible, leaving some overlap risk beyond the explicit algorithm summaries.
The companion repository algorithm claims shortest Fibonacci derivations, so the special-case numerical distance is not presented as independently new apart from the all-seed normal-form theorem.
Unindexed, unpublished or independently discovered free-sector characterizations cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of an invariant, naturally distinguished prefix sector in an iterated rewriting system: exact regular language, uniquely decodable derivations, geodesic length for every target, explicit bivariate growth series and the sharp change at duplication bound four. It upgrades the recent Fibonacci reachability result to an exact optimality-and-uniqueness statement simultaneously for all same-parity pairs, with proof, and explains the phenomenon in a larger seed-independent language rather than by isolated computations. The value does not rely on a paper-sized contribution or speculative downstream applications.
